kaps_punt: Rekkies en vere - ons kan dinge maak beweeg met behulp van uitgerek of verdraai rek en saamgeperste vere; wanneer ons rek uitrek of draai of 'n veer saamdruk, stoor ons energie daarin; wanneer ons die rek of veer vrylaat kry ons bewegings energie

items.bewering: 'n Rekkie lê stil op die tafel en doen niks vanself nie. Jy kan hom uitrek, en jy kan hom 'n paar keer verdraai.
items.blok: Wat jy aan 'n rekkie en 'n veer doen
items.bron: Britannica Dictionary, 'rubber band' (a thin, flexible loop of rubber), https://www.britannica.com/dictionary/rubber-band; twisting as a way of loading a band: SMU propulsion lab, https://s2.smu.edu/propulsion/Pages/proplab.htm

items.bewering: Die klein veer binne-in 'n klikpen is 'n gekrulde draad, en jy kan hom saamdruk.
items.blok: Wat jy aan 'n rekkie en 'n veer doen
items.bron: Make: 'How Does a Retractable Pen Work?' (a compression spring drives the click mechanism), https://makezine.com/?p=500264; Britannica Kids 'spring' (helical spring is wire wrapped in a coil), https://kids.britannica.com/students/article/spring/605269

items.bewering: Jou eie hand doen die werk wanneer jy die rekkie uitrek of verdraai. Daardeur word energie van jou hand in die rekkie gestoor solank jy hom so hou.
items.bron: Study Mind, Elastic Potential Energy (work done stretching an elastic object is stored as elastic potential energy while it stays stretched), https://studymind.co.uk/notes/elastic-potential-energy/; for twisting: SMU propulsion lab, energy stored in a wound band, https://s2.smu.edu/propulsion/Pages/proplab.htm

items.bewering: Van buite lyk dit of niks gebeur nie. Tog trek die uitgerekte rekkie die hele tyd teen jou vingers terug. 'n Slap rekkie trek nie so aan jou vingers nie.
items.bron: Study Mind, Elastic Potential Energy (a stretched elastic object exerts a restoring force that grows with extension; an unstretched one exerts none), https://studymind.co.uk/notes/elastic-potential-energy/

items.bewering: Druk die veer in 'n klikpen plat en jy voel hom terugstoot.
items.bron: Make: 'How Does a Retractable Pen Work?' (the compressed spring pushes back and extends when released), https://makezine.com/?p=500264. Note for the writer, not a fault: a coil spring gets shorter rather than literally flat; 'plat' reads as everyday Afrikaans for squashing it down.

items.bewering: Maak jou vingers oop en die uitgerekte rekkie skiet dadelik weg. Die gestoorde energie word nou bewegingsenergie, en die rekkie self beweeg.
items.blok: Laat los en jy kry beweging
items.bron: Study Mind, Elastic Potential Energy (stored elastic energy is transferred to kinetic energy on release), https://studymind.co.uk/notes/elastic-potential-energy/. Some energy also goes to sound and heat; leaving that out is a fair Grade 5 simplification and matches the CAPS statement.

items.bewering: As jy 'n rekkie verdraai en hom dan laat los, draai hy vinnig terug. 'n Rekkie kan op hierdie manier ook iets anders laat beweeg.
items.blok: Laat los en jy kry beweging
items.bron: US patent 9352241, rubber-band-powered toy vehicle (a twisted band stores energy and untwists to turn a propeller), https://image-ppubs.uspto.gov/dirsearch-public/print/downloadPdf/9352241; RAFT propeller handout (spins fastest just after release), https://raft.net/pgs-propeller-power-chopstick-version

items.bewering: 'n Rekkie spring elke keer terug na sy ou vorm wanneer jy hom laat los. Dit geld solank jy hom nie te ver rek nie.
items.blok: As jy hom te ver rek
items.bron: Elastic limit: the maximum load after which a material still returns to its original shape (VanCleave's Science Fun, https://scienceprojectideasforkids.com/stress-elastic-limit/; University of Houston, Behavior of Materials, https://www.uh.edu/~jbutler/earthsystems/chapter16/tsld003.htm). 'Elke keer' is limited by the next sentence, so the quantifier holds.

items.bewering: Rek jy hom te ver, dan bly hy daarna gewoonlik lank en slap. Hy spring dan nie meer so goed terug nie. Rek jy hom nog verder, dan breek hy.
items.blok: As jy hom te ver rek
items.bron: Natural rubber shows permanent set (it stays longer) and Mullins stress-softening (looser) after a large first stretch: NSF Public Access Repository, https://par.nsf.gov/servlets/purl/10079349; PMC review, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10458811. Breaking with further stretching: same sources and the elastic-limit pages above. 'Gewoonlik' is the right hedge, because how much permanent set remains depends on the rubber.

items.bewering: Sommige vere stoor energie wanneer jy hulle saamdruk. Druk 'n seeppomp se kop af en die klein veer daarin word plat. Laat die kop los en die veer stoot hom vanself weer boontoe.
items.blok: Vere werk nie almal eenders nie
items.bron: Canadian Intellectual Property Office, dispenser pump patent 2544103 (the pump shaft is pressed in against a spring, which returns the dispensing head to its starting position), https://brevets-patents.ic.gc.ca/opic-cipo/cpd/eng/patent/2544103/summary.html. As with the click pen, 'plat' means shorter and squashed, not literally flat.

items.bewering: Die gestoorde energie in die saamgedrukte veer word so bewegingsenergie.
items.blok: Vere werk nie almal eenders nie
items.bron: Study Mind, Elastic Potential Energy (compressed springs store elastic potential energy, which becomes kinetic energy when released), https://studymind.co.uk/notes/elastic-potential-energy/

items.bewering: Ander vere stoor energie juis wanneer jy hulle uitrek. Die vere aan die rand van 'n trampolien rek uit wanneer jy land. Daarna trek hulle weer saam en stoot jou boontoe terug.
items.blok: Vere werk nie almal eenders nie
items.bron: Physics Forums trampoline discussion and tag page (the springs joining the mat to the frame stretch and store energy; trampoline springs are tension/extension springs), https://www.physicsforums.com/threads/how-does-a-trampoline-spring-work.216731/post-1617708 and https://physicsforums.com/tags/trampoline; extension springs store elastic energy when stretched, Study Mind, https://studymind.co.uk/notes/elastic-potential-energy/. Mapping checked: the springs pull together, which pulls the mat tight, and the mat pushes the jumper up. The sentence skips the mat but names the springs' action correctly as pulling ('trek saam'), so it does not teach that a stretched spring pushes. The mat's own stretch also adds to the bounce; the lesson does not deny that.

opsomming: All 22 claims are confirmed (the lesson has no superlatives, and the one comparison-like mechanism, the trampoline springs, was checked for its mapping and holds), so the only thing worth a person's glance is that 'plat' for a squashed coil spring in the click pen and soap pump is everyday wording rather than literal.
